basis: Inflammatory, usually immune-mediated injury of the spinal cord; bladder dysfunction reflects cord injury rather than intrinsic urinary disease.
Encephalopathy, developmental impairment and seizures frequent (30-79%); hepatic failure in 2/2 selected cases does not establish typical-course prevalence.
Subcutaneous fat loss 4/5; cataracts and neurodegeneration define syndrome. Pulmonary/vascular findings (1/2) omitted at cap; pancreatitis is a separate complication.
Congenital absence of a skeletal muscle, with possible foot dorsiflexor weakness.
Photosensitive dermatosis and immunodeficiency define syndrome; insulin resistance and ovarian endocrine failure frequent (30-79%); malignancy risk adds no organ.
B-lymphoblast neoplasm involving blood/marrow or lymphoid tissue; lymphoma component warrants the infectious_immune mechanism axis.
Organic acid metabolism defect; intellectual disability 5/6 and developmental impairment very frequent; dilated cardiomyopathy 5/9.
Inflammation of stomach/intestines; most cases are infectious, particularly viral. No common intrinsic extraintestinal injury.
Gingival inflammation is usually driven by bacterial dental plaque; gums and periodontal soft tissues belong to gastrointestinal.
Meningeal tumour at the upper clivus; skull-base location alone does not establish bone invasion.
Defined autoimmune immune-dysregulation syndrome; leukocyte signalling abnormalities do not establish common damage to any additional organ.
Retinal vascular abnormality and hypogammaglobulinemic immunodeficiency are defining features; retinal vessels are captured by ocular.
Defined by multiple cutaneous steatocystomas and natal teeth; teeth belong to gastrointestinal.
Tumour originates in the sublingual salivary gland, which belongs to gastrointestinal.
GPI biosynthesis defect; severe developmental impairment and delayed myelination documented in 1/1. Sparse hair and contracture lack secure population-level frequency evidence.
Benign proliferation of melanocytic nevus cells within the dermis.
Lysosomal neuronal GM2 storage; retinal/optic degeneration causing visual loss is common in predominant infantile forms (>30% overall); cherry-red spots alone do not qualify.
Definition explicitly includes accelerated severe hypertension, renal failure and papilledema as manifestations of malignant hypertensive organ injury.
Urea-cycle defect; developmental impairment very frequent (80-99%) and progressive spasticity frequent. Single-case hepatic fibrosis/cholestasis does not establish common involvement.
Combined immunodeficiency; no additional organ is consistently directly damaged across most included subtypes. Associated infections are separate diseases.
Permanent tooth agenesis 12/12; intrinsic hair, nail and skin abnormalities occur in approximately 50-67%. Photophobia is below 30% without demonstrated ocular injury.
Germ-cell tumour of the reproductive testis; neither germ-cell origin nor testicular location establishes endocrine disease.
Cytokine receptor dysfunction classified as an immune-system disorder; no specific extraimmune organ injury is established.
ETFB-related MADD; direct lipid-storage myopathy is common (>30%). Cardiac, hepatic and renal injury vary with neonatal severity; subtype-wide frequencies are uncertain.
Inherited cutaneous keratinization disorder with porokeratotic lesions; MVK involvement alone does not establish a systemic metabolic disease.
